text:
### Engagement des parties prenantes

L'engagement des parties prenantes est un aspect clé de la stratégie de l'University of California, Berkeley. Le rapport STARS indique que l'université a mis en place des comités consultatifs pour l'engagement communautaire, qui impliquent des membres de la communauté locale, notamment dans les domaines de la santé publique, de la durabilité et de la justice sociale.

L'université a également établi des comités consultatifs pour la gouvernance, qui impliquent des membres de la communauté locale et des étudiants. Ces comités fournissent aux organisations communautaires un forum pour donner leur avis sur les politiques et les initiatives de l'université qui affectent la population locale.

L'université a également mis en place des partenariats avec la communauté, tels que le programme College Corps, qui a permis à des étudiants de la faculté de participer à des partenariats communautaires dans le domaine de la justice climatique et alimentaire.

Enfin, l'université a mis en place des politiques pour protéger les droits des salariés, notamment en matière de traitement équitable, de procédures de réclamation et d'équilibre vie professionnelle/vie personnelle.

(GRI 2-29)

### Limites et omissions

Ce rapport ne peut pas établir les informations sur les fournisseurs de l'université, les groupes vulnérables ou la méthode d'identification des parties prenantes.

title: Engagement des parties prenantes

evidence.text: Advisory Committees for Community Engagement – UC Berkeley also has various advisory committees and working groups that involve local community members, particularly in areas related to public health, sustainability, and social justice. These bodies provide community organizations with a forum to advise on university policies and initiatives that affect the local population.

Associated Students of the University of California, Chancellor's Office, Student Environmental Resource Center, Zero Waste Coalition, Graduate Assembly, Office of Student Affairs, and the Housing and Dining division all appoint one student seat each on CACS and each have one vote.

Non-academic staff at UC Berkeley can participate in the governance of the institution via advisory bodies of Chancellor's Staff Advisory Committee (CSAC), The Chancellor's Cabinet and other Advisory Commmitees on diversity, sustainability, staff development, and campus services.
The Public Service Center brings together students, faculty, and communities to harness their collective wisdom in support of social justice, civic engagement, and transformative social change.
Sustainability Office, SERC, Government & Community Relations

In {{ EN6_t3_0 }} -, through College Corps, a state partnership funded by California Volunteers, the UC Public Service Center placed undergraduate student Fellows in Climate or Food Justice community partnerships with different community organizations. Each Fellow served for hours over the course of the year, earning $ in living stipends and education awards. Partner organizations included: The Center (Oakland Unified School District's demonstration garden and test kitchen), GRID Alternatives, Frontline Catalysts, Dorothy Day House, Berkeley Meals on Wheels, the Berkeley Student Food Collective, and Climate Emergency Mobilization Task Force, among others.

UC Berkeley Human Resources Policies: UC Berkeley has a dedicated section on its Human Resources website that outlines policies related to employee rights, including fair treatment, grievance procedures, and work-life balance. The policies cover areas like anti-discrimination, whistleblower protection, and employee benefits, offering a transparent overview of employee rights and support. University of California Statement of Ethical Values and Standards of Ethical Conduct: This is a comprehensive code that applies to all UC campuses, including Berkeley.
